mnemonic: 한국 means Korea, but there's more to this little word than meets the eye: its official name is 대한민국 (Republic of Korea), but in casual conversations its citizens use 우리나라 (our country) affectionately when talking about their homeland.
examples: Some bits of history: The English word Korea actually comes from 고려 (Goryeo), an ancient Korean dynasty that stand from 918 to 1392! And before that, the country was ruled by the famous 조선 (Joseon) Dynasty (1392–1897).So 고려, 조선, 대한민국 (1897-1910)... refer to different historical periods of Korea.
- 우리나라는 아름다워요. = Our country is beautiful.
- 저는 한국에 살아요. = I live in Korea.
- 대한민국의 수도는 서울이에요. = The capital of the Republic of Korea is Seoul.

mnemonic: The establishment that serves coffee is said 카페 (sounds just like “café”), meanwhile the product itself is said 커피 (kopi).
examples: I used to confuse 카페 and 커피, maybe a way of saving memory of my primitive Korean-mode-brain. Also because in Spanish I find it hilarious to call the establishment the exact way we call the product and the establishment:
-¡Te veo en el café! = 카페에서 만나요!
(See you in the café!)
-No me gusta el café de ese café. = 저는 그 카페 커피를 좋아하지 않아요.
(I don’t like the coffee from that café.)
See? In spanish it sounds weird to repeat the same word for place and product, so we distinguish it by calling it cafetería = 커피숍 (coffee shop) / 커피 가게 (coffee shop).

mnemonic: 직접 means “directly” or “in person”, and 적 is a suffix that turns a Sino-Korean noun into an adjective-like expression. 직접적 means direct or straightforward. When followed by 으로, it becomes 직접적으로 (directly).
examples: 직접적으로 말해 주세요. = Please speak directly.
그는 직접적인 질문을 했어요. = He asked a direct question.

tr: to speak; to say; to talk
mnemonic: A very common verb. 말 means speech or words, and 하다 means to do. Together, 말하다 literally means “to do speech”, or simply “to speak”. 말하기 is its noun form, meaning speaking.
examples: 한국어로 말해요. = I speak in Korean.
솔직하게 말해 주세요. = Please speak honestly.

mnemonic: Used when avoiding something unpleasant, dangerous, or unwanted. It can refer to avoiding a person, situation, question, or action. 말하기를 피하다 means to avoid speaking.
examples: 어려운 질문을 피했어요. = I avoided the difficult question.
사람들이 죽음에 대해 말하는 것을 피해요. = People avoid talking about death.

mnemonic: Refers to an individual word. Do not confuse it with 문장 (sentence) or 표현 (expression). A useful word when studying languages.
examples: 이 단어의 뜻을 알아요. = I know the meaning of this word.
새로운 단어를 배웠어요. = I learned a new word.

mnemonic: Refers to a way of expressing an idea, feeling, or thought. It can describe a word, phrase, or complete expression. 표현하다 means to express.
examples: 이 표현은 재미있어요. = This expression is interesting.
한국어 표현을 공부해요. = I study Korean expressions.

tr: to be specific; to be particular
mnemonic: 특정 means “specific” or “particular”. The form 특정한 is used before nouns, as in 특정한 단어 (a particular word). It is a Sino-Korean expression.
examples: 특정한 단어를 피하고 싶어요. = I want to avoid a particular word.
특정한 사람을 찾고 있어요. = I am looking for a specific person.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word made from 發 (to produce or emit) + 音 (sound). Literally, it refers to producing a sound. 발음하다 means to pronounce.
examples: 이 단어의 발음은 어려워요. = The pronunciation of this word is difficult.
한국어 발음을 연습해요. = I practice Korean pronunciation.

tr: to be ominous; to be unlucky; to be foreboding
mnemonic: 불길한 describes something that gives a bad feeling or seems to predict misfortune. 불길한 느낌 means an ominous feeling. It is different from simply 나쁘다 (to be bad), because it often suggests something unfortunate may happen.
examples: 불길한 꿈을 꿨어요. = I had an ominous dream.
그 숫자는 불길하다고 생각해요. = I think that number is unlucky.

tr: to recall; to remember; to bring to mind
mnemonic: Used when something comes into your mind or when you intentionally recall a memory, image, or idea. 떠올리게 하다 means to remind someone of something.
examples: 어린 시절을 떠올려요. = I recall my childhood.
이 노래는 고향을 떠올리게 해요. = This song reminds me of my hometown.

mnemonic: A descriptive verb used to compare two or more things. 다른 is its form before a noun, meaning “different” or “another”. Be careful not to confuse it with 틀리다 (to be wrong).
examples: 두 나라의 문화는 달라요. = The cultures of the two countries are different.
다른 방법을 사용해요. = I use another method.

mnemonic: Formed from 죽다 (to die) + 음, a suffix that turns a verb into a noun. 죽다 describes the action of dying, while 죽음 refers to death as a concept or event.
examples: 죽음에 대해 이야기해요. = I talk about death.
그는 죽음을 두려워해요. = He fears death.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word for disease or illness. It is more formal and medical than 병, which is the everyday word for illness.
examples: 이 질병은 위험해요. = This disease is dangerous.
질병을 예방하는 것이 중요해요. = Preventing diseases is important.

mnemonic: 불- is a negative prefix meaning “not” or “un-”, and 편하다 means comfortable or convenient. Together, 불편하다 means uncomfortable or inconvenient. It can describe physical discomfort or an awkward social situation.
examples: 이 의자는 불편해요. = This chair is uncomfortable.
그 질문은 사람들을 불편하게 만들어요. = That question makes people uncomfortable.

mnemonic: A common verb meaning to make or create something. It is also used in the structure -게 만들다, meaning “to make someone feel or do something”.
examples: 저는 케이크를 만들어요. = I make a cake.
그 말은 저를 행복하게 만들어요. = Those words make me happy.

tr: to be like this; to be this way
mnemonic: A descriptive verb used to refer to something that is like this or has this kind of nature. 이러한 is the form used before a noun, meaning “such” or “these kinds of”. Compare 그렇다 (to be like that) and 저렇다 (to be like that over there).
examples: 이러한 문제가 있어요. = There is this kind of problem.
왜 이렇게 어려워요? = Why is it so difficult?

mnemonic: Formed from 언어 (language) + 적 (a suffix meaning “-al” or “related to”). 언어적 means linguistic or related to language. It is commonly used in academic and educational contexts.
examples: 언어적 차이가 있어요. = There are linguistic differences.
언어적 표현을 공부해요. = I study linguistic expressions.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word referring to something that is forbidden or socially prohibited. It can refer to actions, subjects, customs, or words that people avoid.
examples: 그것은 사회적 금기예요. = That is a social taboo.
어떤 문화에는 언어적 금기가 있어요. = Some cultures have linguistic taboos.

mnemonic: Means interesting or fascinating. 흥미 means interest, and 롭다 is a suffix used to form descriptive adjectives. 흥미로운 is the form used before nouns.
examples: 흥미로운 이야기를 들었어요. = I heard an interesting story.
한국 문화는 정말 흥미로워요. = Korean culture is really interesting.

mnemonic: Means an example or instance. 예를 들어 means “for example”. Do not confuse this noun with 네/예, which can mean “yes” in polite conversation.
examples: 좋은 예를 보여 주세요. = Please show me a good example.
예를 들어 설명할게요. = I will explain with an example.

mnemonic: Refers to a number or numeral, especially a numerical symbol. 숫자 4 means the number 4. Compare 수, which can refer more broadly to a number, quantity, or mathematical value.
examples: 숫자 4를 좋아해요. = I like the number 4.
숫자를 읽을 수 있어요. = I can read numbers.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean expression meaning a part of something or some members of a group. It does not mean all. 일부 사람들 means some people.
examples: 일부 사람들은 커피를 좋아하지 않아요. = Some people do not like coffee.
책의 일부를 읽었어요. = I read part of the book.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word for a building or constructed structure. 건 means to build, and 물 is related to an object or thing.
examples: 이 건물은 아주 높아요. = This building is very tall.
건물 안에 엘리베이터가 있어요. = There is an elevator inside the building.

tr: to not exist; to not have; to be absent
mnemonic: The opposite of 있다 (to exist / to have). Korean treats 없다 as a descriptive verb. When describing something that is missing, absent, or unavailable, use 없다.
examples: 시간이 없어요. = I don't have time.
이 건물에는 4층이 없어요. = This building does not have a fourth floor.

tr: instead; in place of; on behalf of
mnemonic: Used when one thing replaces another. The expression A 대신 B means “B instead of A”. It can also mean doing something on behalf of another person.
examples: 커피 대신 차를 마셔요. = I drink tea instead of coffee.
오늘은 제가 대신 일할게요. = I will work on your behalf today.

tr: the letter F; the Latin alphabet letter F
mnemonic: 알파벳 is the Korean word for alphabet, borrowed from the English word “alphabet”. F is the sixth letter of the Latin alphabet. In Korean elevators, F can sometimes be used instead of the number 4.
examples: F는 알파벳의 여섯 번째 글자예요. = F is the sixth letter of the alphabet.
숫자 4 대신 F를 사용해요. = They use F instead of the number 4.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean verb made from 사용 (use) + 하다 (to do). It is a common and slightly formal alternative to 쓰다, which also means “to use”.
examples: 이 앱을 사용해요. = I use this app.
이 단어를 사용하지 마세요. = Please do not use this word.

tr: to mean; to signify; to indicate
mnemonic: Used to explain the meaning or significance of a word, sign, or expression. Do not confuse it with 뜻 (meaning), which is the noun.
examples: 이 단어는 사랑을 뜻해요. = This word means love.
빨간색은 위험을 뜻할 수 있어요. = Red can signify danger.

mnemonic: 한자 refers to Chinese characters used in Korean writing. The term is formed from 韓 (Korean) + 字 (character). Many Korean words have Sino-Korean origins, even when written in Hangul.
examples: 이 단어에는 한자가 있어요. = This word has Chinese characters.
한국어에는 한자에서 온 단어가 많아요. = Korean has many words that come from Chinese characters.

mnemonic: Formed from 유사 (similarity) + 성 (a suffix meaning quality or characteristic). It describes the quality of being similar. It is more formal than 비슷함.
examples: 두 단어의 유사성이 있어요. = There is a similarity between the two words.
발음의 유사성 때문에 혼동할 수 있어요. = You can get confused because of the similarity in pronunciation.

tr: to consider; to regard; to think of as
mnemonic: Used when considering or regarding something in a particular way. The structure A를 B로 여기다 means “to consider A as B”.
examples: 그는 저를 친구로 여겨요. = He considers me a friend.
많은 사람들이 숫자 4를 불길하게 여겨요. = Many people consider the number 4 unlucky.

mnemonic: A native Korean word meaning country or nation. Compare 국가, which is a more formal or official Sino-Korean word for a state or country.
examples: 한국은 아름다운 나라예요. = Korea is a beautiful country.
다른 나라의 문화를 배우고 싶어요. = I want to learn about the cultures of other countries.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean verb formed from 방문 (visit) + 하다 (to do). It is more formal than 가다 when referring to visiting a person or place.
examples: 한국을 방문할 계획이에요. = I plan to visit Korea.
친구의 집을 방문했어요. = I visited my friend's house.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean noun meaning a plan or arrangement. 계획하다 means to plan, and 계획이 있다 means to have a plan.
examples: 여행 계획이 있어요. = I have travel plans.
한국어를 공부할 계획이에요. = I plan to study Korean.

mnemonic: Refers to oneself or one's own person. It often appears in formal writing. Be careful: 자신감 means self-confidence, while 자신 refers to oneself.
examples: 자신을 믿으세요. = Believe in yourself.
자신의 생각을 말해 보세요. = Try expressing your own thoughts.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word meaning attention or caution. 주의를 기울이다 means to pay attention, while 주의하다 means to be careful or watch out.
examples: 운전에 주의하세요. = Be careful while driving.
작은 부분에도 주의를 기울여야 해요. = You must pay attention even to small details.

tr: to direct; to devote; to tilt
mnemonic: Its literal meaning includes tilting something, but in expressions such as 주의를 기울이다 it means to direct or devote attention to something. This is a useful fixed expression.
examples: 주의를 기울이세요. = Pay attention.
그는 공부에 많은 노력을 기울였어요. = He devoted a lot of effort to studying.

mnemonic: A very common adverb used to express the highest degree of something. It is often placed before adjectives or adverbs. Compare 제일, which has a similar meaning and is common in everyday speech.
examples: 가장 좋아하는 음식은 피자예요. = My favorite food is pizza.
이것이 가장 중요해요. = This is the most important.

tr: to be simple; to be easy; to be straightforward
mnemonic: Describes something that is simple, uncomplicated, or not difficult. 간단한 is the form used before nouns. Compare 쉽다 (to be easy), which focuses more on difficulty.
examples: 간단한 질문이 있어요. = I have a simple question.
설명은 아주 간단해요. = The explanation is very simple.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean word meaning culture. It refers to the customs, traditions, arts, beliefs, and ways of life shared by a society.
examples: 한국 문화를 좋아해요. = I like Korean culture.
각 나라에는 다른 문화가 있어요. = Each country has a different culture.

mnemonic: In this context, 면 means an aspect or side of something. It can describe one part of a larger subject. Note that 면 has several other meanings depending on context, including noodles and a district.
examples: 한국 문화의 새로운 면을 배웠어요. = I learned a new aspect of Korean culture.
그 사람의 좋은 면을 봤어요. = I saw the good side of that person.

mnemonic: A versatile noun with several meanings. In the expression -다는 점, it means “the fact that” or “the point that”. It can also mean a point, detail, or score.
examples: 중요하다는 점을 기억하세요. = Remember the fact that it is important.
좋은 점이 많아요. = There are many good points.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean verb formed from 이해 (understanding) + 하다 (to do). It means to understand or comprehend something. 이해할 수 있다 means “to be able to understand”.
examples: 한국어를 이해해요. = I understand Korean.
그 사람의 생각을 이해하고 싶어요. = I want to understand that person's thoughts.

mnemonic: A Sino-Korean adjective formed from 중요 (importance) + 하다. 중요합니다 is its formal polite form, while 중요한 is used before nouns. Compare 중요성 (importance or significance).
examples: 건강은 중요해요. = Health is important.
문화를 이해하는 것이 중요합니다. = Understanding culture is important.
